sourceType: Official Rajasthan Tourism website (Government of Rajasthan)
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: History dates to the 12th century when Rao Deva conquered the territory and founded Hadoti. The independent Rajput state of Kota was carved out of Bundi in 1631; a turbulent history of raids by Mughal rulers, the Maharajas of Jaipur, and Maratha warlords. Known for gold jewellery, Doria sarees, silk sarees, and Kota stone.

places.name: Garh Palace (City Palace)
places.facts: The city's foremost attraction; sprawling complex of suites and apartments built by different Rajput rulers at different times, predominantly Rajput architectural style.

places.name: Rao Madho Singh Museum
places.facts: Houses Rajput miniature paintings of the Kota school, sculptures, arms, and antiques.

places.name: Abheda Mahal and Abheda Biological Park
places.facts: Medieval palace on the banks of a tank, former royal recreation spot; nearby Karni Mata temple; newly built eco-friendly biological park run by the forest department.

places.name: Dad Devi Temple
places.facts: Royal-household deity temple, dedicated to Shri Dad Devi Mata Ji (an incarnation of Durga), surrounded by forest.

places.name: Charan Chauki
places.location: 15 km from Kota, en route to Dad Devi
places.facts: Legendary spot where Lord Krishna is said to have rested while travelling from Mathura to Dwarka; his footprints said to be preserved here.

places.name: Kishore Sagar Jagmandir
places.location: Middle of Kishore Sagar Lake, Kota
places.facts: Built by a Kota queen between 1743-1745; red sandstone island palace; boat rides available; Keshar Bagh nearby known for royal cenotaphs.

places.name: Garden of Joy (City Park)
places.facts: 30-hectare park, 85% intensively planted, with a 1.25 km canal; City Bazaar Amphitheater, Kids Zone, Open Gym, Botanical Garden, Shrubbery Garden, children's boating.

places.name: Chambal River Front
places.location: Kota Barrage to Nayapura Pulia, Kota
places.facts: First heritage riverfront developed in India, 2.75 km along both banks; 26 themed ghats; World Heritage Ghat with replica architecture (Red Fort, Gopuram Temple, Chinese Pagoda, Westminster, Louvre, etc.); fountain and light show; Zodiac ghats.

places.name: Chambal Garden
places.location: Banks of the Chambal River, Kota
places.facts: Popular picnic spot; boat rides near the forest office jetty; part of the National Chambal Gharial Sanctuary, established 1983 to conserve marsh crocodiles and gharials; notable bird population.

places.name: Seven Wonder Park
places.location: Vallabh Bari, along Kishore Sagar Lake, Kota
places.facts: Rs. 20-crore project featuring replicas of the Seven Wonders of the World.

places.name: Khade Ganesh Ji Temple
places.facts: India's only temple with a standing (rather than seated) idol of Ganesh; Rangbadi Balaji temple en route.

places.name: Karneshwar Temple
places.facts: Shiva temple, especially scenic during monsoon; popular with devotees and picnickers.

places.name: Godawari Dham
places.facts: Hanuman temple beside the Chambal River, built entirely of white marble; large marble swan atop the entrance gate.

places.name: Alnia Dam
places.facts: Known for Upper Paleolithic-era rock paintings, still in good condition along the riverbank.

places.name: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
places.facts: Tigers relocated here from Ranthambore; 417 sq km core area plus 342.82 sq km buffer zone; also panther, deer, wild boar, bear.

places.name: Garadia Mahadev
places.facts: Temple with a grand view of the Chambal River and surrounding wilderness, especially scenic during monsoon.

places.name: Kansua Temple
places.facts: One of Kota's oldest temples, dedicated to Shiva; small pond within its premises; stone inscription dated 738 AD attributing construction to Raja Shivgana Maurya, though local legend credits the Pandavas.

places.name: Mathuradheesh Mandir
places.facts: Belongs to the Pushti Marg Vaishnava sect founded by Shri Vallabhacharyaji; Krishna idol brought from Karnaval village near Mathura; major Janmashtami, Nand Mahotsav, Annakoota, and Holi celebrations.

places.name: Gaiparnath Temple
places.facts: Old Shiva temple set in a deep gorge/chasm with a waterfall, scenic views of forests and cliffs.

places.name: Kaithoon
places.facts: Weaver village settled by 'Masuria' families brought from Mysore by Rao Kishore Singh (serving in Shah Jahan's Mughal army); origin of the Kota Doria fabric, originally worn as royal-court turbans, later sarees and dhotis.

places.name: Brajvilas Museum (Government Museum, Kota)
places.location: Brij Vilas Palace, near Kishore Sagar Lake
places.facts: Artefacts from ancient to medieval times: statues (including reclining Vishnu), weapons, manuscripts, coins, sculptures, sacrificial pillars (Yups) of Badva.

places.name: Kishore Sagar Lake
places.facts: One of several lakes commissioned by Kota's rulers; Jagmandir built mid-to-late 18th century as a royal retreat; boat service available to the island palace.

howToReach.air: Nearest airport is Sanganer Airport, Jaipur, ~244 km away
howToReach.rail: Kota is a major junction on the Delhi-Mumbai Western Railway line; most trains pass through Kota
howToReach.road: Regular buses from all cities and towns in Rajasthan
